reasoning: The question asks about short-term movement in 9-month AAA Eurozone government bond yields between Oct 11 and Oct 18, 2026. Evidence shows: ECB raised rates to 2.50% in September, markets expect another hike by December, German yields at multi-year highs (3.49% for 10-year), inflation rose to 3.8%, and energy prices up 19% YoY. The environment is one of rising yields due to inflation concerns and ECB tightening expectations. However, short-term yield movements are noisy. Given the upward pressure on yields from inflation and rate hike expectations, there's a slight bias toward yields increasing, but week-to-week movements are essentially random. I estimate slightly above 50%.
